title: Graduated IO Minimums with Streaming Compression Credits pilot
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Objective: Run a 6-week field experiment that tests a graduated minimum-billing model for per-request IO while introducing a streaming compression credit to better align billing with perceived value for long-running streams. Motivation: customers building chat and live transcription workloads are sensitive to streaming economics and the current flat minimums create disproportionate unit costs for high-ingress low-egress patterns. This pilot explores two levers: 1) Graduated IO minimums that scale the billable floor based on recent directionality (ingress:egress ratio) and average session length, and 2) Streaming compression credits that reduce billable egress tokens for continuous streaming sessions where payloads are highly compressible (subtoken compression heuristics already used in runtime). Hypotheses: - H1: Graduated minimums will increase gross margin on low-margin workloads by at least 2.0 percentage points without reducing paid conversion by more than 3% at cohort level. - H2: Streaming compression credits will drive customer satisfaction (NPS/qual) for real-time apps and will be cost-neutral once backend batching and KV cache benefits are accounted for. Success metrics: delta ARPU, commit upgrades from trial to paid, churn on high-ingress customers, and unit gross margin delta. This ticket covers experiment design, legal/security questionnaire alignment for enterprise changes, pricing copy for Console and docs, and rollout gating with infra feature flags.
acceptance_criteria: Experiment cohorts (control, graduated-minimums, compression-credit) defined and wired in billing simulator
Pricing changes surfaced in Console mockups and reviewed by Design and Sales
Security questionnaire answers updated for enterprise customers (impact to billing logic) and legal sign-off obtained
Engineering has estimated infra, gating, and rollout (feature-flagged by account and region) and provided test checklist
Monitoring dashboards for ARPU, commit conversion, churn, request latency regressions, and billing anomalies are deployed
Experiment runbook documented: duration 6 weeks, minimum sample sizes per cohort, rollback triggers defined

notes: Trade-offs: Graduated minimums increase billing complexity and could confuse customers if not surfaced clearly; mitigated by in-Console calculator and sample invoices.
Risk: If compression credits are overestimated, short-term margin will decline; will use a conservative credit rate (50% of measured compressibility) for the pilot and adjust post-analysis.
Rollout gating: Start with low-risk NA accounts < $5k MRR and a parallel small EU cohort to validate regional parity.
Follow-ups: If successful, we will iterate on a simplified 'streaming-friendly' SKU for public docs and sales quoting tools.
